H6NJ05171.name: Josh Gottheimer
H6NJ05171.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 5th District since 2017; former White House speechwriter, FCC senior advisor, and Ford Motor Company and Microsoft employee.

H6NJ05221.name: Sean Kirrane
H6NJ05221.bio: Entrepreneur and executive with over twenty years in healthcare, finance, and technology; co-founder of the AI governance platform Cortex-X.

positions.stance: Supports restoring the full SALT deduction, eliminating taxes on retirement income, and capping administrative waste in federal programs at 10% with annual audits.
Authored the American Citizens' Primary Residence Mortgage Act, offering temporary federal interest relief and 30- and 40-year fixed mortgages, funded by taxes on speculative and foreign purchases.
Proposes the American Citizens' Health Insurance Act with "universal baseline coverage for all American citizens" and income-based caps on out-of-pocket costs.
Proposes safe private shelter units, mandatory mental health screening and treatment, and a structured path from shelter to housing to independence.
Supports fully funding Gateway Phase 2, including the Secaucus Loop, to deliver "a true one-seat ride into Manhattan" and replace diesel trains with electric rail.

H8NJ03073.name: Frank Pallone
H8NJ03073.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 6th District and Ranking Member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

H6NJ06286.name: Hillary Herzig
H6NJ06286.bio: Former federal civil servant with the U.S. Army, Veterans Administration, USDA, and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services, and former executive assistant to the Key West police chief.

positions.stance: "Hillary will fight for lower property taxes, reduced cost of living, and keeping more of your paycheck in your home."
Supports "safe streets and secure communities without submission to a surveillance state" and limiting the use of law-enforcement technology to spy on Americans.
Supports reducing pollution, protecting drinking water, holding polluters accountable, and standing with local fishermen to safeguard marine life.
Supports congressional term limits, a ban on congressional insider trading, and breaking up monopolies to restore fair competition.
"Healthcare choices belong to families, not government bureaucrats"; says parents must be included in medical decisions affecting their children.

H0NJ07261.name: Thomas Kean Jr.
H0NJ07261.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 7th District in his second term; former New Jersey Senate Republican Leader and General Assembly member.

H6NJ07201.name: Rebecca Bennett
H6NJ07201.bio: Former U.S. Navy helicopter pilot, Air National Guard officer, and healthcare business leader.

positions.stance: Will fully restore the SALT deduction, cut red tape to increase housing supply, pass paid family leave, and fully fund elder care.
Wants New Jersey to lead in clean energy, biotech, and AI; will fund job training and apprenticeships and support workers' right to organize.
Will protect people with pre-existing conditions, restore Medicaid and Medicare cuts, and significantly increase support for mental health services.
Will pass "commonsense, popular gun safety reforms" and "get weapons of war off our streets," while supporting local law enforcement resources.
Will prepare for cyber, drone, and AI warfare and "counter China as the number one strategic threat to global democracy."

H2NJ08232.name: Rob Menendez
H2NJ08232.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 8th District, elected in 2022, serving on the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

positions.stance: Supports restoring the full SALT deduction, creating over 1 million affordable homes, and raising the federal minimum wage to $17.
Will work to expand the Child Tax Credit, cap child care costs at 7% of income for many families, and guarantee universal preschool.
Will advocate to cut greenhouse gas emissions in half by 2030, electrify public transit, and manufacture clean energy technology in the United States.
Will fight to expand background checks to private sales, re-enact and expand the federal Assault Weapons Ban, and address ghost guns.
"Healthcare is a human right"; will fight to protect and expand the ACA, lower prescription drug costs, and codify Roe v. Wade.

H4NJ09194.name: Nellie Pou
H4NJ09194.bio: U.S. Representative; former New Jersey State Senator and Assemblywoman, and former Paterson Director of Human Services and Business Administrator.

positions.stance: Fighting to bring down the costs of housing, groceries, and child care, and called for extending Affordable Care Act tax credits.
Fighting to expand access to health care, lower prescription drug costs, and protect the Affordable Care Act.
Fighting to increase funding for police departments and programs that bolster community safety and trust.
Fighting to protect the VA and veterans' benefits.

H6NJ09264.name: Rosie Pino
H6NJ09264.bio: Clifton City Councilwoman, educator, and founder of multiple nonprofits.

positions.stance: Will "oppose massive spending packages and bureaucratic expansions that fuel inflation"; supports tax cuts for working families and expanding American energy.
Supports protecting people with pre-existing conditions, strengthening Health Savings Accounts, and allowing insurance to be sold across state lines.
Supports fully funding law enforcement and "strongly oppose[s] any effort to defund or weaken the police."
Supports a secure border and legal immigration, and says Border Patrol and ICE should have the tools to arrest and deport violent criminals.
Supports school choice, "including charter schools, education savings accounts, and policies that let funding follow the student."

H4NJ10176.name: LaMonica McIver
H4NJ10176.bio: U.S. Representative for New Jersey's 10th District; former Newark Council President, Montclair Public Schools personnel director, and PSE&G public affairs manager.

positions.stance: Supports universal health care "so that every American can obtain the healthcare they need and deserve at a cost that they can afford."
Supports loans and grants for entrepreneurs in underserved markets, cutting red tape for small businesses, and investing in workforce training and apprenticeships.
Supports addressing mass incarceration, promoting alternatives to incarceration, investing in rehabilitation, and prioritizing restorative justice.
Supports free, high-quality preschool, better teacher pay and smaller classes, and reducing college costs and student debt.
Calls for "common sense gun reform measures, such as universal background checks, closing loopholes in the background check system, and implementing waiting periods."

H4NJ10135.name: Carmen Bucco
H4NJ10135.bio: Small business owner and founder of Bucco's Rising Stars Foundation.

positions.stance: Calls for "standing up for our heroes and demanding the necessary support for our first responders."
"Stopping corruption is a main focus"; says people must be held accountable for their actions.
Supports police and first responders and being "tough on violent crimes"; says the Second Amendment right "should never be infringed upon."
Says schools "must get back to the basics of education" and that school safety should be a top priority.
Says "taxes are out of control" and calls for controlling government spending and stopping frivolous spending.

H6NJ11286.name: Analilia Mejia
H6NJ11286.bio: Union organizer and former director of the New Jersey Working Families Alliance.

positions.stance: "In Congress, I'll make paid sick leave federal law so every worker can care for themselves and their family."
Will re-introduce the Child Care for Every Community Act so families pay no more than $10 a day or 7% of income for child care.
Supports making the first $40,000 in wages free of federal taxes and raising the national minimum wage to $25 an hour.
Will "fight to break up monopolies, block corporate mergers, and cut red tape for small businesses."
Will co-sponsor a moratorium on new AI data centers, make them pay for their energy, and invest in clean energy to lower utility bills.

H6NJ11211.name: Joe Hathaway
H6NJ11211.bio: Randolph Township Council member and 2025 mayor, with over a decade in corporate affairs and communications in healthcare and financial services.

positions.stance: Will support a federal tax freeze and a refundable tax credit for first-time homebuyers during their first years of ownership.
Supports "capping federal student loan interest rates" instead of blanket forgiveness, and major federal investment in vocational and technical training.
Supports expanding the Child Tax Credit, creating a childcare tax credit, and setting guardrails on social media algorithms that target minors.
Will require hospitals and insurers to publish upfront prices, cut out Pharmacy Benefit Managers, and expand Health Savings Accounts.
Will fight to ensure the Gateway Tunnel "is fully funded," prevent construction delays and cost overruns, and expand one-seat ride options to New York City.

H6NJ12417.name: Adam Hamawy
H6NJ12417.bio: Physician and small business owner with a practice in Princeton; former U.S. Army Lt. Colonel and combat trauma surgeon in Iraq.

positions.stance: Supports Medicare for All, "universal, single-payer healthcare with no out-of-pocket costs," and empowering Medicare to negotiate prescription drug prices.
Supports rebuilding the Department of Education, increasing public school funding and teacher pay, universal preschool, and tuition-free public colleges.
Supports abolishing ICE, dismantling DHS, and an "achievable path to citizenship" for undocumented immigrants, including protecting DACA recipients.
Supports at least twelve weeks of national paid family and medical leave, universal childcare, the PRO Act, and taxing wealth.
Supports "significantly cutting the trillion dollar Pentagon budget," reclaiming congressional war powers, and cutting off military aid to human rights violators, including Israel.

H2NJ06210.name: Gregg Mele
H2NJ06210.bio: Has built a career in law, business, finance, technology, and the classroom.

positions.stance: Will fight for responsible budgets, lower barriers to American energy production, and relief from federal rules that raise the cost of housing, food, and business.
Supports legal immigration and will "restore operational control at the border and enforce existing immigration law"; supports police and first responders.
Wants Congress to publish costs, funding sources, and expected results of programs, and audit programs for waste before expanding them.
"Parents are partners—not obstacles—in their children's education"; supports keeping education decisions close to students, families, and communities.
Supports Israel's right to defend its people and "a strong security partnership with Israel"; opposes terrorist organizations and antisemitism.

H8VA01147.name: Rob Wittman
H8VA01147.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 1st District; holds a master's in public health and worked more than 26 years for the Virginia Department of Health.

positions.stance: Fighting for policies that "lower costs, keep taxes down, increase American energy production, reduce unnecessary regulations," and bring manufacturing back from China.
Believes parents, teachers, and local communities should drive education decisions, and supports career and technical education and apprenticeships.
Authored the No Budget, No Pay Act, which withholds members' pay if Congress fails to pass a budget on time, and supports eliminating waste and fraud.
Supports price transparency, Health Savings Accounts, protecting people with pre-existing conditions, and holding insurers and drug middlemen accountable.
Supports investing in roads, bridges, ports, and other infrastructure that "improves safety, reduces congestion," and reaching high-speed internet across the district.

H6VA01299.name: Shannon Taylor
H6VA01299.bio: Henrico County Commonwealth's Attorney (the county's top prosecutor) for 14 years.

positions.stance: Will fight to ban congressional stock trading, proposes 12-year congressional term limits, and will reject all corporate PAC money.
Will fight to restore expired Affordable Care Act tax credits, expand Medicare drug price negotiation, and end surprise medical billing.
Has called for legislation to ensure new data center construction "does not result in increased energy costs for our families."
Will work to pass legislation that takes drugs like fentanyl off the streets and supports law enforcement.
Will fight to cut taxes for working families and small businesses and work to "rein in the reckless tariffs and endless wars" raising prices.

H2VA02064.name: Jen Kiggans
H2VA02064.bio: U.S. Representative and former Virginia State Senator; 10-year U.S. Navy helicopter pilot and primary care adult-geriatric nurse practitioner.

positions.stance: Has prioritized "cutting inflation and lowering the cost of living"; supported making the 2017 tax cuts permanent and expanding the Child Tax Credit.
Supports Trump's efforts to secure the border, including increased border security funding and $47 billion to finish the wall.
Will "never support legislation that weakens law enforcement in Virginia" and opposes efforts to defund or abolish police departments.
Supports a well-funded military and refocusing Defense Department priorities on warfighting and deterrence, believing "global peace can only be achieved through American strength."
Fought to fully fund the Department of Veterans Affairs and supports reducing taxes on military retirement pay and improving post-service employment opportunities.

H6VA02198.name: Elaine Luria
H6VA02198.bio: Former U.S. Representative and 20-year U.S. Navy veteran who founded the Mermaid Factory small business in Hampton Roads.

positions.stance: Will "lead efforts to combat climate change's impact on our local community, fight against offshore drilling, restore the Chesapeake Bay."
Will advocate for strengthening Medicare and Social Security and oppose cuts to these programs.
Supports resources for troops and military families, calls the war in Iran an "unnecessary and endless military intervention," and supports border security with a pathway to citizenship.
Will work to reverse DOGE cuts to veterans' care, cut red tape in the VA system, and ensure veterans get the care they deserve.
Will "fight to repeal the tariffs" and reverse policy decisions that have increased energy costs.

H6VA01117.name: Bobby Scott
H6VA01117.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 3rd District since 1993 and Ranking Member of the House Education and the Workforce Committee.

positions.stance: Fighting "to make sure that all children in America have access to a high-quality public education, regardless of their zip code."
Introduced the Raise the Wage Act and the PRO Act to strengthen workers' right to organize, form a union, and bargain.
Supports Medicare for All and adding "a Medicare-styled public option" to the Affordable Care Act.
Advances evidence-based criminal justice reform; his SAFE Justice Act would effectively eliminate mandatory minimum sentences and expand drug courts.
"Bobby is opposed to any cuts to Social Security and Medicare benefits"; cosponsored the Social Security 2100 Act.

H6VA03121.name: Edwin Rivera
H6VA03121.bio: Former police officer in Puerto Rico and U.S. Army veteran who served combat tours in the Middle East and retired as a disabled veteran.

positions.stance: Supports raising teacher pay, renovating or rebuilding failing schools, funding for HBCUs, and career and technical education pathways.
Supports toll capping and opposes tolls on the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel (HRBT).
"Working families and seniors in CD3 shouldn't have to choose between a prescription and a grocery run."
Supports "expanding mentorship, educational opportunity, and programs that help young people build successful futures."
Supports fully funding law enforcement and community programs, and holding judges and prosecutors accountable for releasing repeat violent offenders.

H4VA04066.name: Jennifer McClellan
H4VA04066.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 4th District on the House Energy and Commerce Committee; former Virginia state senator and delegate.

positions.stance: Fighting "to bring costs down and build an economy that works for everyone," including lower prescription drug prices and more affordable housing supply.
Pushes to expand clean energy and energy efficiency, reduce pollution, and address PFAS "forever chemicals" in Virginia communities.
Defends the Affordable Care Act, pushes to extend enhanced premium tax credits, and opposes Medicaid cuts.
Supports restoring the full protections of the Voting Rights Act of 1965 and opposes the SAVE Act, which she calls "a modern-day poll tax."
Believes "America's strength is amplified by our alliances"; backed a law barring presidents from leaving NATO without congressional approval.

H6VA04129.name: Robert Murray
H6VA04129.bio: Technology executive who founded an IT company and served as IBM's North American CIO Advisory Leader.

positions.stance: Would shift focus "from treatments to prevention," help shore up Medicare beyond 2033, and help veterans get specialized care closer to home.
Would "press to quickly end the wars, restore a 'peace through strength' doctrine," and refocus the military on infrastructure hardening.
Supports cutting energy costs, inspiring entrepreneurship, helping small businesses and farms, and modernizing education to equip the workforce.
Would vote against foreign aid until promises such as Social Security, Medicare/Medicaid, SNAP, CHIP, and WIC are fully funded.
Would "press to prevent governments and corporations from spying on us," saying privacy protects free speech, assembly, and security.

H0VA07133.name: John McGuire
H0VA07133.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 5th District; former Navy SEAL, founder of SEAL Team PT Inc., and former member of the Virginia General Assembly.

H8VA05106.name: Tom Perriello
H8VA05106.bio: Former U.S. Representative for Virginia's 5th District, elected in 2008.

positions.stance: Supports "the best possible path to universal care," whether Medicare for All or alternatives, and aims to save rural health care.
Does not take money from lobbyists or corporate PACs and is running "to shut down the gravy train" of corporate influence over policy.
Would "rebuild federal and fiscal policy around one priority – getting working Americans the raise they've earned."
Supports clearing zoning red tape and permitting delays for starter homes, federal investment in affordable homes, and expanded down payment assistance.
Will "oppose every attempt to hand your benefits to private investors" and says Social Security and Medicare are commitments the country must keep.

H8VA06104.name: Ben Cline
H8VA06104.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 6th District and former prosecutor.

positions.stance: "I will hold Washington accountable by putting an end to wasteful spending and returning as many tax dollars as possible back to the citizens."
Believes "sunshine is the best disinfectant" and supports legislation to increase transparency in government.
"I promise to fight every day to defend the Second Amendment so that we can protect ourselves and our families."
Firmly supports law enforcement officers and opposes "the foolish and reckless proposals to defund the police."
Supports voter ID requirements and ballot safeguards; "it should be easy to vote, but impossible to cheat."

H6VA06173.name: Beth Macy
H6VA06173.bio: Best-selling author and journalist whose books include Dopesick and Paper Girl.

positions.stance: Supports "a nationwide moratorium on new data centers" until energy, environmental, cost, and workforce concerns are addressed, and making Big Tech pay data center costs.
Says Congress should raise the cap on Social Security taxes, encourage zoning reform for affordable housing, and end tariffs.
"I will fight for universal healthcare coverage including Medicare for All."
Says billionaires must pay their fair share, through regulating Big Tech, fairly taxing capital gains, and banning stock trading by members of Congress.
Says "we should double Pell grants" so everyone who wants to go to college can afford it.

H4VA07234.name: Eugene Vindman
H4VA07234.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 7th District; retired 25-year U.S. Army officer, former prosecutor and ethics lawyer, and former National Security Council legal advisor.

positions.stance: His top priority is "cutting taxes and lowering costs for working families"; supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy and warns against reckless tariffs.
Leading efforts to ban members of Congress from prediction markets and lobbying former colleagues; supports banning members from trading individual stocks.
Fighting to lower costs for military families, expand access to health care and mental health services, and ensure veterans receive earned benefits.
Working to lower prescription drug costs, strengthen the Affordable Care Act, and protect Medicare and Medicaid.
Committed to ensuring police and first responders have the funding, training, and tools they need, and to combating the fentanyl crisis.

H6VA07205.name: Doug Ollivant
H6VA07205.bio: U.S. Army combat veteran and former Director for Iraq at the National Security Council.

positions.stance: Supports "a common sense all-of-the-above approach, with small modular nuclear reactors and natural gas at the center."
Supports regenerative agriculture and making it easier for farmers to sell directly to consumers to lower food costs.
Committed to reducing the cost of living, encouraging job creation, cutting red tape for small businesses, and protecting parental rights.
Says governments should increase housing supply by reducing regulation for development and creating legal protections against frivolous zoning disputes, rather than subsidies.
Committed to "easing the tax burden on families and businesses by promoting fiscal responsibility and reducing unnecessary spending."

H4VA08224.name: Don Beyer
H4VA08224.bio: U.S. Representative for Virginia's 8th District in his sixth term, serving on the Ways and Means Committee; former Lieutenant Governor of Virginia and ambassador to Switzerland.

positions.stance: Says "eliminating Trump's tariffs is one of the most effective steps we can take to make life affordable"; champions expanding the Affordable Housing Tax Credit.
Opposes efforts to eliminate the Department of Education and weaken special-needs and Title I programs, and supports relief from student debt.
Sponsors a carbon cap-and-dividend bill returning proceeds to every American, and supports a Green New Deal.
Fights against purges of federal agencies, introduced legislation to facilitate rehiring federal workers, and fought for back pay for furloughed workers.
Sees "diplomatic engagement as the first, second, and third option, with force as a true last resort," while maintaining a strong military.
